messages:
maya (support): FYI customer reported a sudden spike of 502/504s on hosted /v1/streams during peak traffic window (started ~09:20 UTC). They see RST_STREAM + 502 from the gateway. stack: JS SDK 0.12.3, http2=true, long-lived streams (~30s+).

maya (support): Attaching snippet customer sent from their side and a short repro they used:
```
curl -v --http2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"r-big","input":"<large prompt>","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
# Response shows: RST_STREAM 0x1c \n# and then: 502 Bad Gateway (upstream reset)
```

maya (support): customer saw error rate ~6% p95 latency shot up to 5s before the 502s. They disabled retries in their client to avoid retry storms. Asking for quick mitigation and a root-cause path.

lee (sre): Can you paste a minimal SDK example they use? Also did they have many concurrent streams per process? http2 multiplexing + long streams can cause head-of-line issues.

maya (support): their snippet (sanitized):
```
const s = client.stream.create({ model: 'r-big', stream: true });
s.write(prompt);
s.on('data', chunk => {/*...*/});
// They open ~40 streams concurrently from a single host
```

maya (support): they confirmed ~35-60 concurrent streams from one box, typically each ~20-40kb of tokens, lasting 10-40s.

dan (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally by spinning up 50 concurrent long-lived http2 streams -> saw p95 jump and RST_STREAMs from edge when connection pool hit the concurrency limit. Two things jumped out: edge's http2 MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS set low (100) + auth-refresh fanout opened new connections in spikes which caused transient overload. SDK 0.12.3 also aggressively reuses connections without pacing on stream open.

dan (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation: ask customer to set SDK env REDWOOD_HTTP2_MULTIPLEX=false or downgrade to 0.11.x which defaults to HTTP/1 multiplexing. That will force single-stream-per-connection behavior and avoid multiplex head-of-line. Also we can bump edge MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS or increase worker threads as short-term.

maya (support): Passed mitigation to customer: they can toggle env or set http2:false in client options. Will monitor.

lee (sre): I'm going to apply a short-term edge config change: increase per-connection concurrent_streams to 256 for the affected pool, and enable a 1s jitter on auth refresh to reduce connection fanout. Will push change to canary pool first.

sre-oncall: Can confirm canary roll started. watch url: https://internal-canary/redwood/edge/pool-a. Rolling to 10% now.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-8420. Linked ticket: SUP-9312.

maya (support): Customer toggled http2 off and reported immediate improvement: error rate dropped to ~0.4% (from 6%) within 90s. Good short-term.

dan (eng-runtime): Root cause: combination of aggressive connection reuse + long-lived streams + auth-refresh fanout hitting MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS limit at the edge -> connection resets. Fixes in pipeline:
- edge: increase default MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS and add backpressure on stream open
- runtime: small change to auth refresh jitter + staggered refresh (decrease synchronous refresh fanout)
- sdk: release 0.12.4 to add configurable default max concurrent streams and more conservative pacing when stream count is high

dan (eng-runtime): I've opened PRs and a small edge patch. Deploy schedule: canary 12:03 UTC, full pool roll 12:30 UTC if canary looks stable.

maya (support): Customer updated: after canary roll they see sustained <0.5% errors and normal latencies. They're ok leaving http2 off for now but asked for SDK fix so they can re-enable multiplexing.

lee (sre): Canary metrics look good. No spike in 5xx after tweak and auth jitter. Proceeding to full roll.

support-bot: Deployment finished to pool-a at 12:28 UTC. INC-8420 updated.

maya (support): Final customer comms sent: "we applied a temporary edge fix and SDK update is coming; for immediate relief you can set REDWOOD_HTTP2_MULTIPLEX=false or wait for SDK 0.12.4 which will be released later today." They replied :thumbsup: and closed their internal ticket.

maya (support): Follow-ups assigned: update KB about long-lived stream best practices, SDK release notes (0.12.4), and add an internal runbook for auth-refresh jitter. Owner: dan (eng-runtime) / due EOD.

lee (sre): Adding note to postmortem channel after follow-ups done.

maya (support): closing thread, will attach SUP-9312 and INC-8420 to final notes. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
